newsitem.title: FRANCE: BAe's Weston sees link of Aerospatiale, BAe, DASA.
newsitem.headline: BAe's Weston sees link of Aerospatiale, BAe, DASA.

text.p: British Aerospace managing director John Weston told a French parliamentary commission that it was necessary to make a single defence company out of BAe, Daimler-Aerospace and Aerospatiale-Dassault.

In minutes of the Tuesday meeting, published on Wednesday, Weston said such a regrouping was "the strict minimum to create a European company" and added that Italian, Spanish and Swedish firms were also essential partners.
He told the commission, which met behind closed doors, that it was difficult to merge four, five or six companies at the same time but he said a step-by-step approach was possible.
Weston said that the French state's 100 percent stake in Aerospatiale and 50 percent stake in Dassault Aviation, which are slated to merge, would be an obstacle to such a wide-ranging merger.

"It would be very difficult for the management of BAe to propose to their shareholders to exchange the control of 100 percent of their company against a fraction of a European company in which a state would have a major stake," Weston was indirectly quoted as saying.
He envisaged a shell company in which the partners could have a stake and transfer assets at a later stage.
Weston made clear that BAe had no plans to leave the Airbus consortium and despite its recent deal with Lockheed-Martin on the JSF fighter plane, the company had no transatlantic preference.
